data.title: KNOP outlines $225m refinancing and $113m Hedda Knutsen drop-down as distribution rises to $0.075
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: KNOT Offshore Partners (KNOP) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "Revenues were $96.8 million, operating income $15.6 million, net income $3.4 million, adjusted EBITDA $57.6 million," said (CEO & CFO Derek Lowe), adding that available liquidity was "$143.3 million" as of June 30, 2026.

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) reported operational performance of "96.8% utilization, taking into account scheduled dry docking," and said this was "92.4% utilization overall following the dry docking of Fortaleza."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) said KNOP declared "a cash distribution of $0.075 per common unit" paid in August, describing "multiple gradual increases" that are "anchored in our reliable and diversified long-term cash flow and improved balance sheet."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) detailed a post-quarter fleet acquisition: "On September 1, 2026, we purchased the Hedda Knutsen... for a purchase price of $113 million, less an $89.4 million debt facility, plus $0.8 million of capitalized financing fees, resulting in a net cash cost of $24.4 million." He said the deal was negotiated by "our board's independent Conflicts Committee" and noted the vessel is "on time charterer's to Petrobras in Brazil through to November 2034 with an additional 5 years of charter's options."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) highlighted contract and financing actions, including: "the time charter for Hedda Knutsen was executed with Eni to commence in June 2027 for a fixed period of three years plus three charterer's options," and "Time charter for Recife Knutsen was executed by Transpetro to commence in Q3 2026 for a fixed period of two years." He also said KNOP "refinanced" a set of vessels "via a new $225 million 5-year senior secured term-loan facility" at "SOFR plus 165 basis points."

Outlook

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) said market conditions in Brazil and the North Sea are tightening, citing "robust multiyear FPSO pipeline, production growth and continuing investment in exploration and existing project expansion," and added that service-volume increases have been "sustained and sufficient to tighten the supply-demand balance, even as new vessels have been delivered."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) reported backlog of "$881.2 million of fixed contracts" at quarter end, and said KNOP is "fully chartered for the remainder of 2026" with "92% firm coverage or 96% including charter's options" in 2027 and "65% firm coverage, or 93%, including charterer's options" in 2028.

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) stated: "we are well advanced in the refinancing of the $65 million facility secured by the Lena Knutsen, which is due later in October."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) said KNOP removed two prospective dropdowns: "In June 2026, the partnership decided not to pursue the Frida Knutsen and the Sindre Knutsen and they've been removed from our drop-down inventory."

Financial Results

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) summarized Q2 results as "solid financial results" alongside "strong utilization" and reiterated the quarter’s key figures: revenue of $96.8 million and net income of $3.4 million.

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) said liquidity increased versus March 31: "This available liquidity was $2.6 million higher than at March 31," and added that the change was "largely in line with the reducing trend in recent quarters."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) provided borrowing-cost context: "the average margin on our floating rate debt during the second quarter was 2.21% over SOFR."

Q&A

  • Liam Burke, B. Riley Securities, Inc., Research Division: asked whether the Hedda structure implies a different cadence for dropdown growth and whether future dropdown financing could look similar. (CEO & CFO Lowe): "we respond to the offers that are made to us" and said dropdown timing depends on delivery and "the response that the Conflicts Committee wants to make." He added, "the standard model for all of them is that they have a secured debt facility in place already," and said the Hedda debt was "very standard" and that the "$24 million" net cash cost was "fairly consistent" with prior dropdowns.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Slightly positive analyst tone, with limited pressure: Liam Burke opened with "Derek, you've been a busy man this quarter" and focused on mechanics of dropdown cadence and funding rather than challenging results.

  • Management tone was confident and process-driven: (CEO & CFO Lowe) emphasized governance and repeatability of the structure, referencing the "Conflicts Committee" and describing financing as "straightforward" and "very standard" for dropdowns.

  • Versus Q1, the interaction appeared less skeptical and narrower in scope: Q2 featured a single analyst and a single topic (dropdown cadence/financing), while Q1 included multiple analysts pressing on distribution magnitude, macro uncertainty, and revenue movement.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q2 emphasized fleet growth execution and balance sheet actions, led by the Hedda acquisition and the "$225 million" refinancing, whereas Q1 emphasized accounting change: "we changed the useful life estimates of our vessels from 23 years to 20 years" (Q1).

  • Distribution steps accelerated: Q2 declared "$0.075 per common unit" vs. Q1’s "$0.05 per common unit," with Q2 also restating that Q1 was "$0.05" and that it had been "$0.026" for several years before.

  • Backlog and coverage expanded modestly in disclosed figures: Q2 fixed contracts were "$881.2 million" vs. "$858 million" in Q1, with Q2 also providing more explicit 2027–2028 coverage percentages.

  • Analyst focus narrowed in Q2 to dropdown financing repeatability, while Q1 analysts pressed for distribution “magnitude” and asked about macro and fleet aging; management in Q1 declined to provide distribution specifics, while Q2 focused on standardized dropdown mechanics.

Risks and Concerns

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) flagged refinancing execution timing as a near-term item: "we are well advanced in the refinancing of the $65 million facility secured by the Lena Knutsen, which is due later in October."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) framed forward coverage as reliant on option exercise, stating: "Based on current charter rates, we believe charter options are likely to be exercised given the strength of the charter market."

  • (CEO & CFO Lowe) noted utilization was affected by planned off-hire: Q2 utilization included "scheduled dry docking" and specifically referenced "the dry docking of Fortaleza."

Final Takeaway

KNOP’s management presented Q2 2026 as a quarter of steady utilization and contracted cash flows, followed by a material post-quarter fleet addition through the Hedda Knutsen dropdown that management said extends contract runway into 2034 with additional options. Alongside a $225 million refinancing at SOFR plus 165 basis points and an October refinancing in progress for a $65 million facility, Derek Lowe repeatedly framed dropdown execution and financing as standardized and governance-led via the Conflicts Committee, while continuing the stated plan of multiple gradual distribution increases, marked this quarter by a $0.075 per-unit payout.

data.title: Infleqtion initiated with Buy rating due to its full-stack quantum platform: B. Riley
data.description:
B. Riley Securities initiated coverage of Infleqtion (INFQ) with a Buy rating and $23 price target, as it is one of only two publicly traded quantum stocks with a full-stack platform.

Shares inched up 1% during Friday trading.

"We view the entity as one of just two publicly traded quantum names presenting a full-stack platform play with multiple product groups plus an optimized software stack, alongside IonQ (IONQ)," said B. Riley analysts Craig Ellis and Rebecca Zamsky in an investor note.

B. Riley has a Buy rating and $100 price target on IonQ.

"We like an advantaged technology position, as neutral-atom all-to-all gate connectivity lends high logical qubit efficiency and error correction to lift our confidence that already commercial sensing products can add compute systems in a few years," Ellis said of Infleqtion. "Because the same physics underpins sensors and clocks today and likely compute systems ahead, leverage prospects seem compelling inside a large and growing TAM, rising to $16.5B and $35B-$80B in 2030E and 2035E, respectively, with our CY28 and CY29 revenue estimates rising to $75M and $90M."

Infleqtion hit the New York Stock Exchange in mid-February. It has since traded between $8 and $21.  

"Continued volatile sector share action, which often seemingly amplifies AI sentiment, is presenting attractive entry points, in our view, into a steady stream of potential 12-month fundamental and financial catalysts as the industry races toward commercial workload uptake in a few years, which we believe will eventually span all industries," Ellis added. "While early-stage valuation is tricky and with numerous risks to navigate, we believe INFQ has the right ingredients and potential execution to be a long-term quantum winner."

Last week, Infleqtion was awarded a $20M contract from NASA. The follow-on contract is for the continued development of the Quantum Gravity Gradiometer Pathfinder, which is being led by NASA JPL. The Pathfinder is designed to fly the world's first space-based quantum gravity sensor.

data.title: PayPal pauses sale of venture capital portfolio arm - Axios Pro
data.description:
PayPal (PYPL) has paused the planned sale of its venture capital portfolio from ~$900 million to $1 billion.

Offers are said to have come in lower than expected, with the highest bids around 60 cents on the dollar, according to an Axios Pro report on Thursday, which cited multiple unidentified sources. PayPal may have decided that the timing of the sale wasn't ideal, with fintech valuations at depressed levels. 

The update comes after PayPal (PYPL) earlier this year decided to wind down its corporate venture arm, hiring Jefferies to advise on a possible sale. Investments in the portfolio include shopping app Tabby and crypto platform Anchorage.

“As part of our continued efforts to sharpen our focus, we are exploring strategic options for our corporate venture capital arm, PayPal Ventures,” a company spokesperson said in a statement to Fortune in June. 

Shares of PayPal fell 3% on Friday, largely erasing Thursday's 4% gain amid renewed takeover speculation.

data.title: Aclara Resources receives Export-Import Bank LOI for up to $750M
data.description:
Aclara Resources (ARAAF) up 5.3% in Friday's trading after saying the U.S. Export-Import Bank issued a letter of intent indicating it will consider providing as much as US$750M in financing to support the development of the company's Project Dynamo heavy rare earths separation facility in Louisiana.

EXIM indicated that potential financing could cover up to US$750M of project costs with repayment to be completed over 15 years under EXIM's Make More in America initiative, the company said.

Project Dynamo is designed to refine rare earths sourced from Aclara's (ARAAF) mines in Brazil and Chile into high-performance magnet materials that can be used in applications across electromobility, robotics, and other advanced technologies, while also supplying rare earth materials required for power generation applications.

Aclara (ARAAF) said it expects the Louisiana plant to be construction-ready by year-end 2026.

"EXIM's interest in financing our separation, metals, and alloys facility in Louisiana represents a key milestone for Aclara and a strong validation of our strategy to build an integrated mine-to-alloy rare earth supply chain [and] would provide a pathway to bring these capabilities together at industrial scale," CEO Ramon Barua said.

data.title: Tesla's Cybercab launch falls flat; NHTSA launches investigation
data.description:
Tesla’s (TSLA) highly anticipated Cybercab event on Thursday delivered little for investors to digest, with no livestream, no Elon Musk, and no financial details on the company’s robotaxi ambitions.

“We find the lack of direct communication from Tesla as somewhat disappointing with questions as to why the event was not streamed,” said Barclays analyst Dan Levy. “And without any new incrementals on growth/scaling targets, we believe the event could prove to be less significant a catalyst than some investors had expected.”

Heading into the event, Tesla (TSLA) shares were bid higher with the consensus that the launch of the two-seater, fully autonomous vehicle would propel Tesla’s (TSLA) robotaxi ambitions to rival Alphabet’s Waymo (WAYMO). 

But within hours of the Austin launch, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration ((NHTSA)) opened an investigation into the Cybercab’s self-certification against Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards ((FMVSS)), specifically as it relates to the lack of a steering wheel and brake/gas pedals. There is also the added risk of state resistance to the vehicle’s camera-only sensors, all of which caused any remaining post-launch excitement to fizzle.

Regulatory risks aside, the limited scope of the deployment (Austin geofenced) is another weight on Tesla (TSLA) shares Friday morning. But RBC Capital’s Thomas Ito assures investors that concerns about the limited absolute volumes appear “overblown.”

“We reiterate that the deliberately measured pace of the Cybercab fleet rollout reflects an intentional operational strategy rather than any technological constraint,” Ito says, noting that CFO Taneja had explicitly flagged a desire to avoid early-stage service failures.

This strategic deployment hopes to avoid any snafus that could hamper broader consumer adoption as Tesla (TSLA) expands Cybercab coverage to more densely populated cities like Dallas and  Houston.

So with shares in the red on Friday, it seems Wall Street is still uncertain whether Tesla (TSLA) can turn a cautious launch into a scalable autonomous network under NHTSA’s watchful eye.

data.title: Blue Owl plans to create data center REIT, take it public - report
data.description:
Blue Owl Capital (OWL) is looking to create a data center REIT and take it public, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg News.

The proposed company is expected to raise money through an initial public offering and additional share sales, the sources reportedly said.

The REIT could be seeded with ~$6.5B of Blue Owl's own data center assets, according to one of the sources, who asked not to be identified, as the information is private.

OWL shares were 0.93% higher at $11.95 during morning trading on Friday. Other data center REITs were also trading higher (EQIX +0.30% to $1,044.00) and (DLR +0.69% to $189.08).

The AI boom is said to be drawing numerous data center companies into the IPO market.

Blackstone's (BX) newly formed data center REIT, Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC), raised $1.75B in its U.S. IPO after pricing 87.5M shares at $20 each in May.

Brookfield (BN)-backed data center operator, Csquare (CSQR), priced its IPO of 50M shares at $21.00 per share, raising ~$1.05B in its market debut.

data.title: Azenta completes B Medical divestiture as Thelema repays vendor loan
data.description:
• Life sciences company Azenta (AZTA) on Friday announced that it completed the divestiture of its B Medical Systems after Thelema S.à r.l., which acquired the medical refrigeration devices maker in July, repaid a $35M vendor loan related to the deal.
  • Luxembourg-based Thelema completed the purchase of B Medical Systems following a 2025 deal worth $63M, including $35M funded through a short-term vendor loan from an Azenta subsidiary to Thelema.
  • The vendor loan was repaid in full ahead of maturity along with accrued interest, Azenta (AZTA) said, adding that it has released the equity interests tied to the deal, completing the divestiture.
  • "Azenta has now received the entire purchase price in cash, and the credit exposure associated with the transaction has been retired, supporting our disciplined approach to capital allocation,” interim CEO Martin Madaus said.

data.title: Prudential Financial's PGIM launches two core equity ETFs
data.description:
Prudential Financial's (PRU) $1.5 trillion asset management arm, PGIM, has launched two new core equity exchange-traded funds.

The ETFs are the PGIM Jennison Small-Mid Cap Core Equity ETF (PJSM) and the PGIM Jennison International Core Equity ETF (PJIN).

PJSM is expected to invest at least 80% of its investable assets in equity and equity-related securities of small- and medium-capitalization companies.

PJIN is focused on issuers that are non-U.S. companies.

"Core equity investing is often viewed as a choice between active conviction and benchmark discipline, but the reality is that investors don't have to sacrifice one for the other," said Ken Moore, head of Jennison, an investment group within PGIM.

"We draw on decades of bottom-up, fundamental research experience and a global opportunity set to identify opportunities that may be overlooked by purely index-based approaches," added Moore.

data.title: Data center pushback: A key issue for midterms
data.description:
The data center boom is becoming a major issue in the upcoming midterm elections, with local communities pushing back on construction plans amid concerns over electricity rates and environmental impact.

Around 75 data center projects worth about $130B were blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 due to local opposition, according to the Data Center Watch.

And state lawmakers are responding – at least 375 bills on data centers have been introduced this year, The Washington Post's analysis of legislative records found. Around three-quarters of these bills seek to restrict data centers in some way.

According to the National Conference of State Legislatures, 15 U.S. states have considered moratoriums or bans on data centers this year. So far, only New York has passed a one-year moratorium on the construction of large new data centers.

A recent Gallup survey found that seven in 10 Americans oppose constructing data centers for AI in their local area. And candidates running for office in the midterms are latching on to the issue, especially since affordability is now the top issue for voters.

"Candidates in both parties are increasingly running ads against data centers, framing opponents as indifferent to community concerns over their construction," Nicol Lee and Darrell West, both senior fellows in the Governance Studies program at the Brookings Institution, wrote.

"The economy is a central issue in this election, and candidates are therefore packaging affordability, data centers, and electric rate increases into a single narrative and using it to criticize tech development," they added.

Mounting local opposition is driven by concerns over data centers' electricity consumption, water use, land availability and environmental impacts.

Utilities are receiving hundreds of gigawatts in interconnection requests for data centers, which will further strain the power grid. To meet the surge in demand, utilities need to invest more in infrastructure such as power lines and transformers.

And to cover these investments, many utilities are passing on the costs to their customers. 

Meanwhile, large data centers can consume up to 5M gallons per day for cooling servers, according to the Environmental and Energy Study Institute (EESI). That’s equivalent to the water use of a town populated by 10,000-50,000 people.

"Infrastructure bottlenecks, supply chain constraints, uncertainty around AI monetization, growing physical climate risks, regulatory hurdles and community opposition will increasingly determine where and how AI infrastructure is built," Allianz Commercial said.

Notable hyperscalers: Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), Google (GOOG) (GOOGL), Meta (META), Oracle (ORCL), CoreWeave (CRWV).

data.title: DNO drops takeover bid for Genel Energy after scooping up Capricorn
data.description:
Genel Energy (GEGYF) plunged 14.6% in London trading Friday after Norwegian oil and gas operator DNO (DTNOF) (DTNOY) said it will not make an offer to acquire its British peer.

In August, DNO (FTNOF) (FTNOY) made a 69 pence/share takeover approach that valued Genel (GEGYF) at £202M, which the U.K. company dismissed on the grounds that it "fundamentally undervalues" the business; since then, DNO said Genel has "demonstrated no willingness to engage."

Under U.K. takeover rules, DNO (DTNOF) (DTNOY) had until September 4 to announce a firm intention to make an offer for Genel (GEGYF) or walk away.

Earlier this week, DTO (DTNOF) (DTNOY) trumped a bid by Genel (GEGYF) for Capricorn Energy, agreeing on a deal that valued the British oil and gas E&P company at $396M; Genel had previously reached an agreement to acquire Capricorn for ~$360M.
